generic_extensions_used: env config + entrypoint/args override (binary run directly; the stock entrypoint needs root to create OS users)
setup steps: SQL via psql exec, nonce-cookie form login, session cookie, admin reload, API-user token capture
http oracle on a different service (external sink) with a settle policy

app_specific_workarounds.what: run ./listmonk directly with an install-then-serve shell command instead of the stock entrypoint
app_specific_workarounds.why: the entrypoint creates OS users (needs root)

app_specific_workarounds.what: SMTP target and root URL set with one SQL UPDATE of the settings table, then the app's own admin reload
app_specific_workarounds.why: Listmonk stores SMTP settings in the DB; its settings API needs a read-modify-write the contract language does not express

AM1_assumption: 200 from /api/tx means ACCEPTED for sending, not delivered: the success<=>commit assumption is not guaranteed; it held in every observed run only because delivery completed within the settle window
AM4_native_late_commit: yes: the app acknowledges (200) and delivers asynchronously (accepted-then-late-commit exists natively; not injected)

browser_D6.level: B0 for this action: POST /api/tx has no UI (API-only, by design)

read_back: none: Listmonk exposes no user-visible record of sent transactional mail; a verification-based policy can never confirm and always abstains
D3_independence_note: oracle L3 (external sink); the cross-check source is a second Mailpit endpoint (same store), so D3 shows counting consistency, not independent agreement

fidelity_D2.lost_ack: F2 for API clients (503 to the client, exactly one email delivered)
